extracted.intended_audience: readers, writers, and editors interested in short stories and anthology selection
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and editorial criteria visible in an anthology introduction and contemporary reviews that indicate what makes a short story selection successful (voice, aural qualities, originality, momentum, variety). Useful for anthology editors and short-story writers seeking what editors/reviewers value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice of the story (speaking voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: “I’ve spoken of 'the voice of the story,' which has become a sort of catchall phrase; but by it I intend something more specific: a speaking voice, like the singing voice in music, that moves not across space, across the page, but through time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atwood treats 'voice' as a primary, specific criterion: a story's written text functions as a 'score for voice' and must be re-translated into sound to work. Emphasis on a distinct, time-moving 'speaking voice' as central to a story's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story as a score for voice / necessity of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: “Surely every written story is, in the final analysis, a score for voice. Those little black marks on the page mean nothing without their re-translation into sound.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorially value stories that imply or sustain an oral/audible performance — the text should suggest how it will 'sound' when read aloud. This frames selection toward pieces with strong performative/audible qualities rather than purely visual or strictly structural merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection by listening / learning from others' voices
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of her essay ... she states 'From listening to the stories of others, we learn to tell our own.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection process described as an act of listening; editors may prioritize stories that teach or model voice. Implies a pedagogical/editorial preference for pieces that contribute to a living tradition of storytelling and influence writers' own voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for the aural tradition (vs. minimalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nona Balakian (NYT) writes that 'what lends a family likeness to most of the 20 writers in this volume is their preference for the aural tradition. It proves a refreshing change from a tired minimalism that has prevailed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers praise works that favor an aural/sonic storytelling lineage; this is presented as an evaluative standard in contrast to valuing 'minimalism.' Editors/reviewers may reward richness of sound, oral qualities, and a tradition that privileges voice and aurality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Momentum via variety of approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers Weekly noted 'this anthology is, for the most part, unusually compelling. Atwood and series editor Ravenel's 20 selections achieve momentum via a variety of approaches.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthology-level criterion: selections should collectively generate momentum and sustain reader interest, achieved through diversity of techniques, tones, and approaches. Editors should balance pieces so the collection feels dynamic rather than monotonous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of angle and attack; avoid predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Reviews criticizes that many selections are 'less than stellar and often quite predictable in angle and attack' while praising a few that 'stand out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers reward distinctive perspectives and surprising 'angle[s]' or 'attack[es]' on subject matter. Predictability is flagged as an anti-pattern; editors and writers should seek freshness in approach and execution to make stories stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong work of voice can distinguish a story
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus also notes that, although many stories are 'mild and conventional,' two of those short stories 'weigh in with strong works of voice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even within a generally conventional selection, exceptional voice can elevate a story. This reinforces voice as a high-leverage criterion: distinctive vocal presence can compensate for other conventional aspects of plot or theme.
